Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 14, "heading": "CHAPTER 12. LIKING LIFE ON MY OWN ACCOUNT NO BETTER, I FORM A GREAT RESOLUTION", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u014-b0030", "target": "Но сквозь всю ту смуту и угнетённость духа, в которую мы оказались, как мне казалось, неожиданно вовлечены, я ясно разглядел, что мистер и миссис Микобер и их семейство уезжают из Лондона и что расставание между нами близко. Именно по дороге домой в тот вечер и в бессонные часы, которые затем последовали, когда я лежал в постели, мне впервые пришла мысль — не знаю, как она пришла мне в голову, — которая позднее оформилась в твёрдое решение.", "source_sha256": "20e893594170252914fd9950af943caa1d0ad034ca1d6e93e798091c11ba5ecb", "target_id": "ru-en85-u014-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "c24255ea30c58e73378df550e91b8970aff6521b3c7416f8f39ef99b9e786474"}, {"source_id": "en85-u014-b0031", "target": "Я так привык к Микоберам, был так близок с ними в их бедах и оставался без них таким совершенно одиноким, что перспектива искать какое-нибудь новое пристанище и снова оказаться среди неведомых людей была подобна тому, как если бы меня в эту самую минуту выбросили в мою нынешнюю жизнь, уже с тем готовым знанием о ней, какое мне дал опыт. Все чувствительные струны, которые она так жестоко ранила, весь стыд и все страдания, которые она поддерживала живыми в моей груди, стали острее, когда я думал об этом; и я решил, что такая жизнь невыносима.", "source_sha256": "b6e6e8dc417ff8227164b0dcc006913e5cb18c88bd5d313a076a4d7350d5b8e0", "target_id": "ru-en85-u014-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "945f2a44e87309fcc184641754811192f3fd3d5dc2f23bb1fd6543cc97e4b54d"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 12, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u014-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "That there was no hope of escape from it, unless the escape was my own act, I knew quite well. I rarely heard from Miss Murdstone, and never from Mr. Murdstone: but two or three parcels of made or mended clothes had come up for me, consigned to Mr. Quinion, and in each there was a scrap of paper to the effect that J. M. trusted D. C. was applying himself to business, and devoting himself wholly to his duties—not the least hint of my ever being anything else than the common drudge into which I was fast settling down.", "sha256": "3d2ef18b288fdd415d1fce1b9b335a8d90c8f715e7f94e6cd1f5f2ec5e72a8b8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[32]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The very next day showed me, while my mind was in the first agitation of what it had conceived, that Mrs. Micawber had not spoken of their going away without warrant. They took a lodging in the house where I lived, for a week; at the expiration of which time they were to start for Plymouth. Mr. Micawber himself came down to the counting-house, in the afternoon, to tell Mr. Quinion that he must relinquish me on the day of his departure, and to give me a high character, which I am sure I deserved. And Mr. Quinion, calling in Tipp the carman, who was a married man, and had a room to let, quartered me prospectively on him—by our mutual consent, as he had every reason to think; for I said nothing, though my resolution was now taken.", "sha256": "76db160a290395410a03559ddeea498de11a641badf8d536127513ba49dfe7e3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I passed my evenings with Mr. and Mrs. Micawber, during the remaining term of our residence under the same roof; and I think we became fonder of one another as the time went on. On the last Sunday, they invited me to dinner; and we had a loin of pork and apple sauce, and a pudding. I had bought a spotted wooden horse over-night as a parting gift to little Wilkins Micawber—that was the boy—and a doll for little Emma. I had also bestowed a shilling on the Orfling, who was about to be disbanded.", "sha256": "56f80ceae88569a941efe24667615d193aaead467979bad8ae6918eeb627d0a0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We had a very pleasant day, though we were all in a tender state about our approaching separation.", "sha256": "d8bda2a14178324cada394c68f1d45efcf6b9f404846880cd6f735c04e9c371f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I shall never, Master Copperfield,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘revert to the period when Mr. Micawber was in difficulties, without thinking of you. Your conduct has always been of the most delicate and obliging description. You have never been a lodger. You have been a friend.’", "sha256": "666d944719467964583e9ee9686e9783be126941134e890a88007007cddd00b5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear,’ said Mr. Micawber; ‘Copperfield,’ for so he had been accustomed to call me, of late, ‘has a heart to feel for the distresses of his fellow-creatures when they are behind a cloud, and a head to plan, and a hand to—in short, a general ability to dispose of such available property as could be made away with.’", "sha256": "29d928ca53a35fc889b18a68992f439801ebb7f64e2755b5d80f0435754ceb76", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I expressed my sense of this commendation, and said I was very sorry we were going to lose one another.", "sha256": "3e5fa9e27b2300bbec5b9543b534f58d48c4277ef2250e84ddbb445e96e3fa5e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[38]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear young friend,’ said Mr. Micawber, ‘I am older than you; a man of some experience in life, and—and of some experience, in short, in difficulties, generally speaking. At present, and until something turns up (which I am, I may say, hourly expecting), I have nothing to bestow but advice. Still my advice is so far worth taking, that—in short, that I have never taken it myself, and am the’—here Mr. Micawber, who had been beaming and smiling, all over his head and face, up to the present moment, checked himself and frowned—‘the miserable wretch you behold.’", "sha256": "4c99e34b89cb3376f1e8ab2686c4d41a007bf85f6b80a9d71221a28937892d83", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear Micawber!’ urged his wife.", "sha256": "5e432449ef685f8add7da2e2f06addbfc6e8e313214007702fab699ddbfad093", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I say,’ returned Mr. Micawber, quite forgetting himself, and smiling again, ‘the miserable wretch you behold. My advice is, never do tomorrow what you can do today. Procrastination is the thief of time. Collar him!’", "sha256": "2e183ab882943e76f03f8c2008722b10eed2cc8d3ca1cecf3fb687380f3b780d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My poor papa’s maxim,’ Mrs. Micawber observed.", "sha256": "a654b512d161044923c96983e8b075149e47c2daced3d30072c51a5f8c583a2e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear,’ said Mr. Micawber, ‘your papa was very well in his way, and Heaven forbid that I should disparage him. Take him for all in all, we ne’er shall—in short, make the acquaintance, probably, of anybody else possessing, at his time of life, the same legs for gaiters, and able to read the same description of print, without spectacles. But he applied that maxim to our marriage, my dear; and that was so far prematurely entered into, in consequence, that I never recovered the expense.’ Mr. Micawber looked aside at Mrs. Micawber, and added: ‘Not that I am sorry for it. Quite the contrary, my love.’ After which, he was grave for a minute or so.", "sha256": "96b489357ef5ac921ecd387c45a50d0c62eb6c91b13fd3c8ef843f160c43a19a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My other piece of advice, Copperfield,’ said Mr. Micawber, ‘you know. Annual income twenty pounds, annual expenditure nineteen nineteen and six, result happiness. Annual income twenty pounds, annual expenditure twenty pounds ought and six, result misery. The blossom is blighted, the leaf is withered, the god of day goes down upon the dreary scene, and—and in short you are for ever floored. As I am!’", "sha256": "44e535618276ba3f8dae825ac937c4c8096eeb0e273f462ebf53db2dd40e80f1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "To make his example the more impressive, Mr. Micawber drank a glass of punch with an air of great enjoyment and satisfaction, and whistled the College Hornpipe.", "sha256": "d40a4a60ea3dbb0d53ff739f71fe2c6c5ec6e34c369a0eb5c6de9be4c347d198", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[45]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I did not fail to assure him that I would store these precepts in my mind, though indeed I had no need to do so, for, at the time, they affected me visibly. Next morning I met the whole family at the coach office, and saw them, with a desolate heart, take their places outside, at the back.", "sha256": "0a4c48417f86a7feea513550f48e287bc355124c72a8288e59bed617827a7f63", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Master Copperfield,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘God bless you! I never can forget all that, you know, and I never would if I could.’", "sha256": "6aa4cdb80d1e6f395a2a3d70f701c5be9ad0ae1d2d1e3c3e4a60b16c663812ed", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Copperfield,’ said Mr. Micawber, ‘farewell! Every happiness and prosperity! If, in the progress of revolving years, I could persuade myself that my blighted destiny had been a warning to you, I should feel that I had not occupied another man’s place in existence altogether in vain. In case of anything turning up (of which I am rather confident), I shall be extremely happy if it should be in my power to improve your prospects.’", "sha256": "023b91e5fbb2798055a620b561461a476e1b01bfc10c76c8b1cb42c24687b719", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I think, as Mrs. Micawber sat at the back of the coach, with the children, and I stood in the road looking wistfully at them, a mist cleared from her eyes, and she saw what a little creature I really was. I think so, because she beckoned to me to climb up, with quite a new and motherly expression in her face, and put her arm round my neck, and gave me just such a kiss as she might have given to her own boy. I had barely time to get down again before the coach started, and I could hardly see the family for the handkerchiefs they waved. It was gone in a minute. The Orfling and I stood looking vacantly at each other in the middle of the road, and then shook hands and said good-bye; she going back, I suppose, to St. Luke’s workhouse, as I went to begin my weary day at Murdstone and Grinby’s.", "sha256": "5824deeaa93e598e14f67f3989ae63eb4452555dc9cf6398f9bddc348cafa008", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But with no intention of passing many more weary days there. No. I had resolved to run away.—-To go, by some means or other, down into the country, to the only relation I had in the world, and tell my story to my aunt, Miss Betsey. I have already observed that I don’t know how this desperate idea came into my brain. But, once there, it remained there; and hardened into a purpose than which I have never entertained a more determined purpose in my life. I am far from sure that I believed there was anything hopeful in it, but my mind was thoroughly made up that it must be carried into execution.", "sha256": "78fb52d0148278b4180899d84bcadd49262e4ac95519efbf728cb13ddc17b559", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Again, and again, and a hundred times again, since the night when the thought had first occurred to me and banished sleep, I had gone over that old story of my poor mother’s about my birth, which it had been one of my great delights in the old time to hear her tell, and which I knew by heart. My aunt walked into that story, and walked out of it, a dread and awful personage; but there was one little trait in her behaviour which I liked to dwell on, and which gave me some faint shadow of encouragement. I could not forget how my mother had thought that she felt her touch her pretty hair with no ungentle hand; and though it might have been altogether my mother’s fancy, and might have had no foundation whatever in fact, I made a little picture, out of it, of my terrible aunt relenting towards the girlish beauty that I recollected so well and loved so much, which softened the whole narrative. It is very possible that it had been in my mind a long time, and had gradually engendered my determination.", "sha256": "0d1fa951ce63a5b7879a24d6f010a4090b922df3a586e5060dd61ebb173eb560", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As I did not even know where Miss Betsey lived, I wrote a long letter to Peggotty, and asked her, incidentally, if she remembered; pretending that I had heard of such a lady living at a certain place I named at random, and had a curiosity to know if it were the same. In the course of that letter, I told Peggotty that I had a particular occasion for half a guinea; and that if she could lend me that sum until I could repay it, I should be very much obliged to her, and would tell her afterwards what I had wanted it for.", "sha256": "94fa0385f812082cae183398cea8e2b85b244bb54a197bf729065e887b063b07", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Peggotty’s answer soon arrived, and was, as usual, full of affectionate devotion. She enclosed the half guinea (I was afraid she must have had a world of trouble to get it out of Mr. Barkis’s box), and told me that Miss Betsey lived near Dover, but whether at Dover itself, at Hythe, Sandgate, or Folkestone, she could not say. One of our men, however, informing me on my asking him about these places, that they were all close together, I deemed this enough for my object, and resolved to set out at the end of that week.", "sha256": "c6231873a78fc102a41247234f7b4a973530fdb26633bec62bdc1242296db8ed", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Being a very honest little creature, and unwilling to disgrace the memory I was going to leave behind me at Murdstone and Grinby’s, I considered myself bound to remain until Saturday night; and, as I had been paid a week’s wages in advance when I first came there, not to present myself in the counting-house at the usual hour, to receive my stipend. For this express reason, I had borrowed the half-guinea, that I might not be without a fund for my travelling-expenses. Accordingly, when the Saturday night came, and we were all waiting in the warehouse to be paid, and Tipp the carman, who always took precedence, went in first to draw his money, I shook Mick Walker by the hand; asked him, when it came to his turn to be paid, to say to Mr. Quinion that I had gone to move my box to Tipp’s; and, bidding a last good night to Mealy Potatoes, ran away.", "sha256": "cebefebbbf72d727b84679713f3722ced656c0df230ad90ea6e810e2bcb58148", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My box was at my old lodging, over the water, and I had written a direction for it on the back of one of our address cards that we nailed on the casks: ‘Master David, to be left till called for, at the Coach Office, Dover.’ This I had in my pocket ready to put on the box, after I should have got it out of the house; and as I went towards my lodging, I looked about me for someone who would help me to carry it to the booking-office.", "sha256": "1bbf9b7cebb9cac5b96ea4427b42c3e5bb9efdfaf9427c38cb166e8183cf5796", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "There was a long-legged young man with a very little empty donkey-cart, standing near the Obelisk, in the Blackfriars Road, whose eye I caught as I was going by, and who, addressing me as ‘Sixpenn’orth of bad ha’pence,’ hoped ‘I should know him agin to swear to’—in allusion, I have no doubt, to my staring at him. I stopped to assure him that I had not done so in bad manners, but uncertain whether he might or might not like a job.", "sha256": "c5c0f6dd4a49514093f80e1ee496977a4ff49f447e87ab57564b536f86506eb4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Wot job?’ said the long-legged young man.", "sha256": "ce2dd777f3b9801ef13c43eb4eb421547e3761726021f1ad02b129c70ba1ab0c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To move a box,’ I answered.",
